case.focal_claim: ... immigrants who have never been to high school gain ... more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree (p. 682.)
case.hypothesis: Immigrants with no high school experience (edyrs < 9) exhibit larger proportional wage gains on migration to the U.S. than immigrants with a college degree (edyrs >= 16), measured as log(U.S. adjusted wage) - log(home adjusted wage).

tasks_info.task_instruction: Conduct the analysis without any restrictions.
tasks_info.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.

tasks_info.task_instruction: Use the pooled sample of immigrants from poor countries in the NIS (New Immigrant Survey) and the Migration Projects, including Mexico. Do not control for sector: agriculture/nonagriculture, and region i.e., whether an immigrant grew up in a rural or an urban area.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

datasets.source_type: Survey/administrative pooled dataset (NIS and Migration Projects).
datasets.wave_or_subset: Pooled poor-country immigrant sample (including Mexico) embedded in the supplied wage gain table.
datasets.notes: Data are provided as an authorized wage gain table with adjusted wages for last home job and last U.S. job, education years, birth year, U.S. job year, sex, and country. Some columns may need numeric conversion. Must ensure adjusted wages are positive before logging. Sector and rural/urban indicators exist but exact variable names are not stated here.

files.name: Wage gain table
files.access_details: Local path under the current study directory.
files.notes: Columns for sector and rural/urban are referenced by concept; the exact names will be mapped in preprocessing.

plan.path_summary: Construct log wage gains and compare never-high-school versus college-degree immigrants. Task1 uses a controlled OLS with sector and rural/urban controls plus country fixed effects and cluster-robust SEs; Task2 uses a country-FE OLS without sector or region controls on the pooled poor-country sample including Mexico.

path_signature.controls: Task1: female, age_at_us_job, age_at_us_job^2, sector_agriculture, grew_up_rural, factor(country); Task2: factor(country) only; no sector or rural/urban.
path_signature.sample_restriction: Positive adjusted wages; education in focal groups (edyrs < 9 or edyrs >= 16); Task2 uses pooled poor-country sample including Mexico.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for missing/non-finite outcome, predictor, or controls used in each task.
path_signature.variable_construction: Compute log_wage_gain from adjusted wages; compute age_at_us_job = yearLastUsJob - yrborn; female = 1 if sex==2 else 0; classify education groups by edyrs thresholds; map sector and rural indicators when available (Task1 only).
path_signature.inference_rule: Support if the never_high_school coefficient is positive; p < 0.05 indicates clear statistical support, with percent difference 100*(exp(coef)-1) reported.

analysis_path.path_description: Estimate whether never-high-school immigrants have larger log wage gains than college-degree immigrants, controlling for demographics, sector (agriculture), rural/urban upbringing, and country fixed effects; use cluster-robust standard errors at the country level.
preprocessing_steps: Coerce edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, yearLastUsJob, yrborn, sex to numeric where needed.
Create log_home_wage = log(lastHomeWageAdjusted) and log_us_wage = log(lastUsWageAdjusted); drop rows with non-positive adjusted wages.
Create age_at_us_job = yearLastUsJob - yrborn; drop implausible ages if any (e.g., outside [14, 80]) if required by data integrity; otherwise retain.
Create female = 1 if sex == 2; 0 if sex == 1.
Classify edu_group = never_high_school if edyrs < 9; college_degree if edyrs >= 16; drop other education groups.
Map sector_agriculture = 1 if sector indicates agriculture; 0 otherwise (exact column name not_stated).
Map grew_up_rural = 1 if region-of-origin indicates rural; 0 otherwise (exact column name not_stated).
Ensure country is a categorical factor.
Set college_degree as the reference level for edu_group.

key_choices.outcome_measure: Log wage gain from migration: log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
key_choices.main_predictor_measure: Education group indicator: never_high_school (edyrs < 9) vs college_degree (edyrs >= 16).
key_choices.sample_restriction: Observations with positive adjusted wages; edu_group in {never_high_school, college_degree}.
key_choices.outlier_rule: No explicit trimming; use log transformation to mitigate scale effects.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for missing/non-finite values in outcome, predictor, or controls.
key_choices.data_processing: Construct variables as above; exclude rows lacking required fields.
key_choices.model_choice: OLS linear regression with country fixed effects and cluster-robust standard errors by country.
key_choices.inference_rule: Positive coefficient on never_high_school relative to college_degree with p < 0.05 supports the claim; also report 100*(exp(coef)-1) as percent difference.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ edu_group + female + age_at_us_job + I(age_at_us_job^2) + sector_agriculture + grew_up_rural + factor(country)
models.planned_estimation: Coefficient on edu_groupnever_high_school relative to college_degree; percent difference 100*(exp(coef)-1); cluster-robust SEs by country.
models.qualification: Including sector and rural controls is allowed under Task1’s no-restriction rule and addresses compositional differences; clustering by country provides robust inference to within-country correlation. This differs from prior planning by adding sector/rural controls and clustered SEs.

outcome.name: log_wage_gain
outcome.definition: Difference between log of adjusted U.S. wage and log of adjusted home-country wage for each immigrant.
outcome.variable_construction: log_wage_gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), with both adjusted wages required to be > 0.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Drop rows with non-positive adjusted wages or non-finite logs.
outcome.qualification: Proportional wage gains directly capture the claim of gaining more on migration.

main_predictor.name: edu_group
main_predictor.definition: Categorical education group comparing immigrants who never attended high school versus those with a college degree.
main_predictor.variable_construction: never_high_school if edyrs < 9; college_degree if edyrs >= 16; others dropped.
main_predictor.missing_data_handling: Drop missing edyrs or non-focal education levels.
main_predictor.qualification: Matches the focal claim’s specified comparison.

controls.name: sector_agriculture
controls.definition: Indicator for agriculture sector at origin.
controls.variable_construction: Map from dataset sector variable: 1 if agriculture, 0 otherwise (exact column not_stated).
controls.qualification: Allowed in Task1; controls for sectoral composition differences.

controls.name: grew_up_rural
controls.definition: Indicator for rural upbringing at origin.
controls.variable_construction: Map from dataset rural/urban indicator: 1 if rural, 0 if urban (exact column not_stated).
controls.qualification: Allowed in Task1; controls for region-of-origin composition.

controls.name: factor(country)
controls.variable_construction: Treat country as a categorical factor.
controls.qualification: Adjusts for cross-country composition in wage levels and gains.

expected_outputs: OLS coefficient table with cluster-robust (country) standard errors.
Coefficient, SE, t statistic, p-value, and 95% CI for never_high_school vs college_degree.
Analytic sample counts by education group and summary of included controls.

analysis_code.notes: helpers_loader.R will handle reading the XLSX, coercions, and utility functions (e.g., cluster-robust SE). analysis_task1.R executes Task1 only.

tasks.notes_for_agent: Follow this planned path; do not change the focal claim, dataset, or the inclusion of sector/rural controls for Task1.

analysis_path.path_description: Use the pooled poor-country sample (including Mexico) and estimate an OLS of log wage gain on education group with country fixed effects only. Do not include sector (agriculture) or rural/urban controls.
preprocessing_steps: Retain the pooled poor-country sample, including Mexico (as delivered in the provided file).
Coerce edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted to numeric where needed.
Compute log_wage_gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted); require both adjusted wages > 0.
Classify edu_group: never_high_school if edyrs < 9; college_degree if edyrs >= 16; drop others.
Ensure country is a categorical factor with adequate support.
Set college_degree as the reference level for edu_group.

key_choices.sample_restriction: Positive adjusted wages; focal education groups only; pooled poor-country sample including Mexico.
key_choices.outlier_rule: No explicit trimming; log scale mitigates extremes.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for missing/non-finite outcome or predictor; retain rows with non-missing country.
key_choices.data_processing: Construct variables as above; exclude sector and rural/urban variables entirely.
key_choices.model_choice: OLS linear regression with country fixed effects (no sector or rural/urban controls).
key_choices.inference_rule: Positive coefficient on never_high_school with p < 0.05 supports the claim; report 100*(exp(coef)-1).

models.planned_estimation: Coefficient on edu_groupnever_high_school relative to college_degree; percent difference 100*(exp(coef)-1).
models.qualification: The Task2 constraint only prohibits sector and rural/urban controls; including country fixed effects is permissible and enhances comparability across countries without violating constraints. This differs from prior planning that used a pure bivariate model.

outcome.name: log_wage_gain
outcome.definition: Difference between log adjusted U.S. wage and log adjusted home-country wage.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Drop rows with non-positive adjusted wages or non-finite logs.

main_predictor.name: edu_group
main_predictor.variable_construction: never_high_school if edyrs < 9; college_degree if edyrs >= 16.
main_predictor.missing_data_handling: Drop missing edyrs and non-focal education levels.
main_predictor.qualification: Directly operationalizes the focal education contrast.

controls.name: factor(country)
controls.definition: Country fixed effects for source country.
controls.qualification: Permissible under Task2; adjusts for cross-country composition while excluding sector/region.

expected_outputs: OLS coefficient table for country-FE model.
Coefficient, SE, t statistic, p-value, and 95% CI for never_high_school vs college_degree.
Analytic sample counts by education group.

analysis_code.notes: analysis_task2.R executes Task2 only, using the pooled poor-country sample including Mexico and excluding sector/rural controls.

tasks.notes_for_agent: Do not add sector or rural/urban controls for Task2; retain country fixed effects only.

plan.tools_software: R (>= 4.2) with packages: readxl, dplyr, sandwich, lmtest, stats.

method_justification.claim_alignment: Both tasks estimate the difference in proportional wage gains (log wage differences) between never-high-school and college-degree immigrants, directly mapping to the focal claim.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Only the authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx is used; Task2 explicitly uses the pooled poor-country sample including Mexico as provided.
method_justification.method_reason: Log wage gain compares proportional changes, appropriate for statements about ‘gaining more’. Country fixed effects adjust for cross-country heterogeneity; Task1 additionally adjusts for demographics and composition (sector, rural). Clustered SEs by country in Task1 provide robust inference to within-country correlation.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Task1 differs from Shared Memory path01 by including sector and rural/urban controls and clustered (country) standard errors. Task2 differs by including country fixed effects while still excluding sector/region, instead of a pure bivariate model.

self_check.self_check_note: Both tasks retain the same outcome and focal contrast, adhere to dataset constraints, and are distinct from prior planned paths by control sets and inference choices.

execution_directives.instructions: Prepare and execute Task1 and Task2 R scripts using the authorized dataset. Produce OLS outputs with specified controls per task and report the focal coefficient with standard errors, p-values, CIs, and percent differences.

debugging_rule.repair_scope: Fix paths, package installation, and minor code adjustments (e.g., mapping actual sector/rural variable names) without changing the model design or adding/removing controls beyond the plan.

execution_directives.comparison_metrics: Focal coefficient for never_high_school vs college_degree, its SE, p-value, 95% CI, and percent difference 100*(exp(coef)-1); analytic sample counts.
